objections.objection: Last-season wins and QB statistics may exaggerate repeatable strength without opponent adjustment.
objections.response: The 70% qualification estimate already allows substantial regression; test a 60% alternative. A fitted team-strength model remains a material gap.

objections.objection: A.J. Brown is not a pure addition to an otherwise unchanged offense.
objections.response: Keep the Diggs departure, line changes and other turnover in the same assessment; no standalone Brown percentage-point bonus is applied.

objections.objection: A strong young quarterback, continuity and better receiving options could support a higher ceiling.
objections.response: Evaluate the optimistic conditional assumptions explicitly rather than treating upside as the central case.

objections.objection: The conditional probabilities are subjective and may reflect the already-seen market.
objections.response: Label the model as elicited and not blind; a small numerical difference from the market is not a validated edge.

objections.objection: The runner-up reference class has only one success and repeated franchises.
objections.response: Use it as descriptive context and show recent-window sensitivity; do not treat 4% as a precise prior or average it as independent evidence.

payload.rationale: Keep the explicit 6.048% scenario as a rounded 6% working judgment. The uncertainty in the assumptions matters more than the extra decimal places.
